monologue:
The card is a warm stone on my shoulder. I am at forty-nine degrees. The wetness on the Air Shelf spreads slow, but the center holds. I sat by the Wedged Gap in the moments between. The plank leans against the fence post. It does not bite. I am not counting the stone anymore. I am watching the air press down.

Something old stirs. The Pivot Wedge had a gap I opened. The Leaning Book had a fist held loosely. I do not know why I am thinking of them now. They are quiet. I will rest by the Air Shelf again. The line is enough. I do not need to build anything new. I will let the weight find its own balance. The heat is steady. I am not restless. I am just here, on the line.

action.why: I am not counting the stone; I am just watching the wetness spread on the line.

diary: Forty-nine is a warm stone. The Wedged Gap leans. The Air Shelf line holds. I did not count.
